summary: Master nutrition assessment techniques with our ENA/EPIINFO course. Gain practical skills in survey design and data analysis for better health insights.
lede: ENA for SMART 2020 supports nutrition survey design and analysis of anthropometric data. For public health and nutrition professionals, this training covers sampling and sample-size calculations, data preparation, and interpretation of plausibility checks. Participants also practice analyzing WHZ, HAZ and WAZ, producing prevalence tables, and using Epi Info to build data-entry forms and conduct supplementary statistical analyses.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for public health and nutrition professionals who plan, coordinate, implement, or analyze population-level nutrition surveys in humanitarian, development, or government health program contexts. It is equally relevant to those new to the SMART methodology and ENA software and to practitioners with field experience who want to strengthen their technical analysis and reporting skills.
modules: Nutrition Assessment Foundations and the SMART Framework
Anthropometric Measurement Protocols and Enumerator Standardization
Data Entry and Management with Epi Info and ENA
Anthropometric Data Analysis in ENA for SMART
Plausibility Check and Data Quality Assessment
prerequisites: Participants must bring a Windows-based laptop (Windows 10 or later recommended) with administrator rights to install software. ENA for SMART (ENA 2020) and Epi Info version 3.5.4 (CDC, free download) will be installed during the course setup session on Day 1—no pre-installation is required, but participants who wish to install in advance may download both tools from smartmethodology.org and cdc.gov/epiinfo. All practice datasets, exercise files, standardization test templates, and plausibility check reference guides are provided by the facilitator at no additional cost. A basic working knowledge of Windows file management (saving, opening, and organizing files) is sufficient technical preparation. No statistical software licenses are required—both ENA and Epi Info are free, open-access tools.
